zara: Blocking on docs PR #599 — I added a migration note and example that sets `batching.buffer_ms: 5` and says "requests will wait up to 5ms to form a batch". Preview passed but runtime folks: is that strictly true?
michael: can you paste the config snippet?
zara: snippet: 
```
serving:
  batching:
    enabled: true
    buffer_ms: 5
    max_batch_size: 64
```

zara: PR text currently claims: "buffer_ms controls how long the router buffers requests to form batches (default 5ms)."
ash: putting merge on hold until we confirm. My concern: the runtime has adaptive behavior — buffer_ms is a hint and there's a target-latency heuristic.
michael: right. The docs should not promise a hard ceiling. Also note platform-level overrides for Dedicated/Private that clamp buffering to meet SLOs.
runtime-bot: Clarification from runtime:
- `buffer_ms` is a per-deployment hint for the router's batching window (default: 5ms when not set).
- Runtime uses adaptive batching: it will shorten or lengthen the window based on recent throughput and the configured `target_token_latency`.
- Under low throughput the router may extend beyond `buffer_ms` to aggregate economically; under high throughput it may use sub-ms windows.
- Admins can enable `deployment.policy.force_static_batching=true` to make `buffer_ms` strict (not recommended for multi-tenant Dedicated setups).
- Compatibility note: quantized kernels and KV cache flush semantics can affect effective batching (see parenthetical in the guide).

zara: thanks. Can you suggest a one-line replacement for the docs so we don't overpromise?
michael: "`buffer_ms` is a per-deployment hint for the router's batching window; the runtime adapts the actual window based on workload, token-latency targets, and admin policy overrides."
ash: also add a short bullet on precedence: 1) deployment.policy.force_static_batching 2) deployment.batching.buffer_ms 3) runtime adaptive heuristics.
ci-bot: preview deployed for PR #599  https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr/599 (status: success) :white_check_mark:
zara: added the wording + tiny precedence bullets and a short SDK example showing how to inspect effective batch stats. Pushed. PTAL.
michael: LGTM, wording is accurate without being prescriptive.
ash: ack from docs reviewer. Approving after runtime-bot ack.
runtime-bot: acked. Small note: include parenthetical about quantization/seq-len when explaining batching compatibility.
docs-bot: label "merge-on-runtime-confirmation" added by docs-bot.
